note.backdrop: A quiet open after Nvidia's report. At 8:34 ET the S&P 500 fund was +0.2%, the Nasdaq 100 fund +0.6%, small companies -0.4% and the VIX -3.3%: big technology up, the rest flat. Oil -2.4% and gold -2.4% moved most; TradingKey puts gold below $3,800 an ounce and silver -3% to $45.73, and says signs of improving Middle East supply weighed on oil (WTI $83.24, Brent $92.39). The day's scheduled news: the Federal Reserve's October minutes this afternoon and Anthropic's offering price tonight, first trade Thursday (Yahoo Finance; TradingKey says Anthropic told investors to expect the top of its range or higher, citing Bloomberg). Only 3 of 2,449 stocks were outside their 9-in-10 range and 10 outside their 2-in-3 range, and four of those rest on one or two early prints (see unexplained).

read.says: Before the open: Nasdaq 100 futures +0.81%, S&P 500 futures +0.31%; gold down more than 2% below $3,800, silver -3% to $45.73, oil about -2% on signs of improving Middle East supply; Nvidia nearly +3%, Dell over +5%, Coherent over +6%; Applied Optoelectronics nearly -10% on an at-the-market plan to sell up to $550 million of stock; TSMC nearly +4% on reports of foundry price increases from early 2027, unconfirmed.

S&P 500 futures +0.3%, Nasdaq 100 futures +0.8% after two days of falls; Anthropic expected to price tonight; Target's third quarter: sales +7.1% to $27.1 billion (estimate $26.5 billion), diluted EPS $2.65 (estimate $2.08) including a $0.50 benefit from tariff refunds, comparable sales +5.6%, shares lower before the open; Fed minutes today.

Ardent Health priced a secondary offering of 8,000,000 shares (7,136,719 from an affiliate of Equity Group Investments, 863,281 from an affiliate of Ventas) at $14.50, with a 1,200,000-share option; the company will buy back 1,500,000 of them from the underwriters at their price, from cash; it sells no shares and receives nothing.

Ecovyst's board appointed a director as interim chief executive effective November 17, replacing the chief executive, who is departing and will consult until February 5, 2027; no reason given; fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 guidance of November 5 reaffirmed; a search for a permanent chief has begun.

BellRing's fourth quarter: net sales $692.0 million (+7%), net earnings $35.6 million, adjusted EBITDA $66.4 million after a $16 million inventory charge; fiscal 2026 sales $2,398.4 million and adjusted EBITDA $288.8 million after $37 million of inventory headwinds; fiscal 2027 outlook: sales $2.32-$2.42 billion and adjusted EBITDA $310-$350 million.

singles.beneath: In proportion: $14.50 is 18.3% below Tuesday's close of $17.75, and the stock has moved to the offering price, as Vir did last week. At $17.75 the company was worth about $2.5 billion, about 141 million shares; 8 million is 5.7% of them, 4.6% net of the buyback, and 6.5% with the option. A discount that deep on a sale by holders, not the company, is unusual; my reading is that buyers asked a large concession for a large block, and the upsizing says the holders accepted it. The company receives nothing; the buyback costs about $21 million of its $766 million cash.
singles.cause: Ardent Health priced the secondary offering it announced after Tuesday's close at $14.50 a share, upsized to 8 million shares from 7 million, sold by affiliates of Equity Group Investments and Ventas; the company buys back 1.5 million of them at the underwriters' price (its pricing release; Investing.com). The stock is -19.7%.

singles.beneath: Reaffirming guidance in the same release says the change is not about this year's numbers, but a departure effective the day before the announcement, with no successor and no reason, leaves the reason open; my reading is that the market charges for that uncertainty. About $110 million of value on a $1.1 billion company. Its chemical partners did not move.
singles.cause: Ecovyst's chief executive is departing; a director became interim chief effective November 17, with no reason given, and the company reaffirmed its 2026 guidance (its 8-K). The stock is -10.0%.

singles.beneath: In proportion: the sales guide's middle, $2.37 billion, is 1.2% below fiscal 2026's $2,398.4 million; the EBITDA guide's middle, $330 million, is 14% above $288.8 million, but fiscal 2026 carried $37 million of inventory charges, and without them it was $325.8 million, so the guide is about flat. The stock was 67% below its 52-week high, so a flat year with no new cut is better than what that price assumed; that is my reading. The company also named a new finance chief.
singles.cause: BellRing reported fourth-quarter sales of $692.0 million (+7%) and guided fiscal 2027 to sales of $2.32-$2.42 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $310-$350 million; Zacks counts a 4.8% earnings beat and 6.0% sales beat (its release; Zacks). The stock is +14.4%.

singles.beneath: A chief-executive change the same morning as Ecovyst's, in a different industry; the two are not connected. I did not read why the change was made. Its payments-software partners did not move.
singles.cause: ACI Worldwide appointed an interim chief executive (its release). The stock is -4.4%.

singles.beneath: A results report from a $1.7 billion company; I did not read past the headline figures, so what the market liked is not established here.
singles.cause: J&J Snack Foods reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $33.6 million (its 8-K; AP). The stock is +4.9%.

singles.beneath: Without the refund, EPS was $2.15, 3% above the estimate: most of the headline beat is a one-time refund, which is why a 27% beat moved the stock so little. That the refund explains the muted reaction is my inference; the sales and comparable-sales beats are real.
singles.cause: Target reported sales of $27.1 billion (+7.1%, estimate $26.5 billion), comparable sales +5.6% and diluted EPS of $2.65 against an estimate of $2.08, including a $0.50 benefit from tariff refunds (Yahoo Finance). The stock is -0.5%.

singles.beneath: An at-the-market program sells into the market over time, so the dilution arrives gradually; $550 million is a ceiling, not a sale. It filed at 4:06 ET, minutes before Nvidia reported, so the optics rally that followed did not prompt it. It was among the scan's likeliest 20%+ days before the filing.
singles.cause: Applied Optoelectronics filed to sell up to $550 million of stock over time through an at-the-market program (TradingKey; its 424B5 and 8-K after Tuesday's close). The stock is -10.3%.

themes.beneath: In proportion: Nvidia at about $160.18 at 8:36 ET is 1.7% below its Nov 13 close of $162.89, where the desk's size call started; it needs a close at or above $175.11 or at or below $150.67 on Friday for that call. The report answered whether spending is still rising; it did not answer the questions the strategist names (returns on the spending, how it is financed, Nvidia's leadership). TradingKey adds that Nvidia has halted shipments of licensed Hopper products to China. TradingKey also reports foundry price increases from early 2027, unconfirmed: if they come, the chip designers here pay more for the same wafers (untested; TSMC is not in the scan).
themes.cause: Nvidia's beat and raise lifted the AI build-out after Tuesday's close; by 8:34 ET most of the group kept less than half of it. Nvidia +4.8% after hours, +2.6% now; CoreWeave +9.0% to +3.0%; IREN +10.1% to +3.4%; Coherent +7.2% to +3.4%; Lumentum +6.5% to +2.6%; Vertiv +6.4% to +2.0%; Dell +6.2% to +2.6%; Marvell +5.7% to +1.9%; Micron +4.7% to +1.6%; Oracle +4.1% to +1.5%; AMD +3.9% to +1.7%; Broadcom +2.9% to +1.9% (the last note's after-hours reads; this check's reads). TradingKey's figures at 7:30 ET (Dell over +5%, Coherent over +6%) sat between the two, so the fade ran through the morning.
themes.mechanism: Nothing new was reported against Nvidia overnight; the stocks gave back gains as more traders priced them. The same names had fallen most on the spending worry, so they swing most both ways. Yahoo Finance's Asia report quotes a strategist: an initial relief rally without the conviction for a sustained recovery (an opinion). That the fade is sellers using the bounce, not new information, is my inference.
themes.name: Half of the AI build-out's after-hours gains gone before the open
themes.watch: Whether the group closes above or below this morning's level. A close back near Tuesday's lows says the report changed little; a close at the after-hours highs says the morning was noise. Anthropic's price tonight is the next test of what investors pay for AI.

themes.beneath: One root for both, which is my inference: easing Middle East risk takes the war premium out of oil and the safe-haven premium out of gold at once. The dollar's +0.3% is its usual day and does not explain a 2.4% gold fall on its own. Gold below $3,800 and Brent at $92.39 are the levels TradingKey reports.
themes.cause: Gold -2.4% and oil -2.4% since the close, each beyond its usual day for gold (1.8%) and inside it for oil (3.6%). TradingKey reports gold below $3,800 and silver -3%, and says improving Middle East supply weighed on oil. The gold and silver miners' median fell 4.0% (10 stocks): Newmont -3.4%, Hecla -3.6%, Coeur -3.3%, Royal Gold -3.3%, Barrick -1.6%.
themes.mechanism: A miner's costs barely move with the metal, so its profit moves more than the metal's price: a 2.4% fall in gold took about 4% off the median miner, about 1.7 times as much. Royalty companies such as Royal Gold have no mining costs but fell as much, so the pull is the metal itself.
themes.name: Gold and oil fell together; gold miners fell more
themes.watch: If Middle East supply news reverses, both should rise together; if gold falls while oil holds, the common root is wrong.
